Save on Wedding Photos & Video – Book Fewer Hours and Order the Album Later

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (411 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that book your wedding photographer from the ceremony through the first dance, toasts, and cake, and a videographer for the ceremony and toasts or not at all.
  • For couples who married in 2025, a photographer cost an average of $3,000 and a videographer $2,300, according to The Knot 2026 Real Weddings Study.
  • Each hour of coverage adds to the price, and so do the extras.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that book your wedding photographer from the ceremony through the first dance, toasts, and cake, and a videographer for the ceremony and toasts or not at all. Take digital files you’re free to print instead of an album package, and hire a newer pro whose complete wedding galleries you’ve seen, not a friend with a camera.

For couples who married in 2025, a photographer cost an average of $3,000 and a videographer $2,300, according to The Knot 2026 Real Weddings Study.

Each hour of coverage adds to the price, and so do the extras. Many photographers charge separately for a second shooter, the extra photographer who works alongside the first. An album sold on its own can add several hundred dollars. The moments worth paying for fit in a few hours: the ceremony, family portraits, the first dance, the toasts, and the cake cutting.

Book coverage from the ceremony through the cake cutting, and add the getting-ready hours only if you want those photos. Ask your DJ to schedule the first dance, toasts, and cake early in the reception. Skip the second shooter for a small wedding, where one photographer can cover it all. For video, book just the ceremony and toasts, or skip it.

In a recent development, for a lower rate, look at newer photographers building a portfolio, or ask photographers what they charge for a Friday, Sunday, or winter date. Judge each by two or three complete wedding galleries, not a portfolio of best shots, and get a contract listing the hours, the overtime rate, when the files arrive, and your print release. Even a newer pro beats a friend with a camera, since a friend signs no contract and is a guest that day too.

According to recent reports, ask each photographer you like to quote both the full package and five hours with files only. The difference is what the extra hours and the album cost you.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that price what you sell on eBay from what the same item sold for, not from what other sellers are asking.
  • A regular eBay search highlights only listings still for sale, so its prices are what sellers hope to get.
  • Search for your item and check Sold items in the filters to see the last 90 days of sales.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that price what you sell on eBay from what the same item sold for, not from what other sellers are asking. Run an auction only for something rare or in high demand, list everything else at a fixed price that takes offers, and build a small item’s postage into its price so you can offer free shipping.

A regular eBay search highlights only listings still for sale, so its prices are what sellers hope to get.

Search for your item and check Sold items in the filters to see the last 90 days of sales. Price yours near the middle of the five most recent sales of the same model in the same condition.

An auction suits only something rare or in high demand, where competing bidders can push the price up. Give everything else a fixed price with Best Offer turned on, so buyers can propose a lower one.

Then make the listing easy to find and trust:.

According to recent reports, in most categories, eBay keeps 13.6% of the buyer’s total up to $7,500, sales tax and any shipping charge included, plus $0.40 on each order over $10. Buy postage through eBay Labels, which sells USPS, UPS, and FedEx labels below retail rates. Build that postage into a small item’s price and offer free shipping. For a heavy one, charge calculated shipping, which varies with the buyer’s location.

Promoted listings, eBay’s paid ads, take 2% or more of the sale, at a rate you set, whenever the item sells in the 30 days after anyone clicks the ad. Save them for a common item among many identical listings.

Industry observers note that say you’d have priced a vintage camera lens at $110, it ships for $12 on an eBay label, and its last five sales ran $148 to $169, with $156 in the middle. At $156 with free shipping, you net about $122 after eBay’s fee and the label, about $40 more than the $83 you’d net at $110. Set the minimum offer at $148, the lowest of those sales, and eBay declines anything lower for you.

To decide whether eBay is the right place for what you sell, read our eBay review, or compare it with the best Craigslist alternatives for selling your stuff.

Tech Report: Amelia Earhart Search Find Trees, Not Plane. Mystery Remains

📅 21 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (436 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A highly anticipated expedition to solve one of aviation’s greatest mysteries has concluded without finding the wreckage of Amelia Earhart’s missing plane.
  • A 17-person team from the Archaeological Legacy Institute and Purdue University recently returned from Nikumaroro, a remote and uninhabited atoll in the Pacific Ocean.
  • Industry observers note that their primary objective was to investigate the Taraia Object, a mysterious shape in a shallow lagoon that researchers first noticed in 2020 on satellite and historical aerial photos.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A highly anticipated expedition to solve one of aviation’s greatest mysteries has concluded without finding the wreckage of Amelia Earhart’s missing plane.

A 17-person team from the Archaeological Legacy Institute and Purdue University recently returned from Nikumaroro, a remote and uninhabited atoll in the Pacific Ocean.

Industry observers note that their primary objective was to investigate the Taraia Object, a mysterious shape in a shallow lagoon that researchers first noticed in 2020 on satellite and historical aerial photos. While some hoped the anomaly was the remnants of Earhart’s Lockheed Electra, the expedition determined it was entirely natural.

Sources indicate that the Taraia Object on a satellite image. Located at Nikumaroro. Photo: Archaeological Legacy Institute.

According to Purdue University officials, the object was a cluster of large fallen trees resting on a sandbar. Much of the debris observed in satellite images had already broken up and washed away, leaving a single Y-shaped piece. The reflective, metallic glint seen from above turned out to be a hardened layer of coral sand coating the wood.

Industry observers note that on the way to the atoll. Photo: Purdue Research Foundation.

Industry observers note that the five-day operation proved logistically complicated. Workers faced dense brush and a large population of giant coconut crabs. The nocturnal activities of the massive crabs forced the crew to abandon looks to camp on the atoll and to return to the ship each evening. During the day, the crabs simply minded their own business.

One of the crew holds a coconut crab. Photo: Purdue Research Foundation.

Despite the difficulties, researchers recovered a few minor artifacts to study lagoon drift patterns, including a 76cm steel tube.

The team emphasized that ruling out the Taraia Object does not disprove the broader “castaway hypothesis.” For decades, historians have investigated the theory that Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan drifted off course during their 1937 global circumnavigation attempt, landing on Nikumaroro’s reef after failing to find Howland Island.

Amelia Earhart. Photo: amelia.prf.org.

Purdue University, where Earhart once served as a career counselor and aviation advisor, stated that its commitment to the search remains unchanged.

Sources indicate that “Amelia Earhart never gave up — she kept pushing boundaries and flying into the unknown,” remarked Steve Schultz, Purdue’s general counsel and field assistant, after the expedition. “She kept flying, and we will keep searching.”.

For more details, extensive project documentation, and a gallery of expedition photographs, you can visit the official mission site at Amelia.prf.org.

According to recent reports, from left to right: Steve Schultz, Sirisha Bandla, and Marc Hagle, members of the research team. Photo: Purdue Research Foundation.

Join a nonprofit’s lending circle when you need a small loan but have little or no credit history. Members pay in each month and take turns collecting the pot, so nobody pays interest, and the nonprofit reports every payment to the credit bureaus. Your payments continue until the last member collects, so pick an amount you can always pay.

A payday loan commonly costs $15 per $100 borrowed, an annual percentage rate of almost 400% on a two-week loan, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau states. A lending circle charges 0% interest, though you get the money only when your turn comes.

Sources indicate that it’s the same arrangement as a tanda, a susu, or a hui. In a 10-person circle paying $100 a month, a different member takes the $1,000 pot each month. Going first gets you an interest-free $1,000 loan, and going last works like saving $1,000.

Sources indicate that in an informal circle among friends, a member who stops paying after collecting leaves the others short, and nobody’s payments count toward their credit. Mission Asset Fund (MAF), a San Francisco nonprofit, has members sign loan documents, collects payments electronically, and reports them to all three major credit bureaus. In MAF’s version of that example, all 10 members would add 10 on-time payments to their credit reports.

In a recent development, MAF’s circles have 6 to 12 members, loans of $300 to $2,400, and typical monthly payments of $50 to $200. Applicants take its online financial education courses, then settle on a loan amount and their place in the order, so ask for an early turn if you need the money soon.

To apply with MAF directly, you need to be 18 or older, live in California, and have:.

Sources indicate that MAF’s partner nonprofits run circles in more than a dozen other states and Washington, D.C. Where none is near you, a credit-builder loan also builds a payment history, at a small cost.

Sources indicate that in that 10-person circle, the first member still owes nine $100 payments after collecting, and a missed one can hurt the credit history you joined to build. Pick a loan amount whose payment you could make every month of the circle, not just until your turn.

#44954. Mortgage REITs Pay Double-Digit Dividends on Borrowed Money – Keep Your Stake Small

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (497 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Moneycrashers ↗ Open Full Page

Mortgage REITs Pay Double-Digit Dividends on Borrowed Money – Keep Your Stake Small

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (497 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mortgage real estate investment trusts (REITs) often yield 10% or more by borrowing several dollars for every dollar of their own to invest in mortgages.
  • In a recent development, recent yields run higher still.
  • Unlike REITs that own buildings, a mortgage REIT owns mortgages or bonds made from them and earns the difference between the interest they pay and its own borrowing costs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mortgage real estate investment trusts (REITs) often yield 10% or more by borrowing several dollars for every dollar of their own to invest in mortgages. So a jump in interest rates can cut both the payout and the share price. If you buy one, keep it a small slice of your portfolio and hold it in an IRA.

In a recent development, recent yields run higher still. An index of mortgage REITs from Nareit, the REIT industry group, yielded 16.59% at the end of October 2026, against 1.04% for the S&P 500.

Unlike REITs that own buildings, a mortgage REIT owns mortgages or bonds made from them and earns the difference between the interest they pay and its own borrowing costs. Agency mortgage REITs buy bonds whose payments Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, or Ginnie Mae guarantee, then borrow heavily against them. Annaly Capital Management, which holds mostly agency bonds, ended September 2026 with borrowing and commitments to buy bonds equal to 5.9 times its net worth, its third-quarter report shows. Commercial mortgage REITs make property loans that carry no such guarantee.

When rates jump, mortgage bonds lose value and the borrowing costs more, and shareholders take the loss on everything bought with borrowed money. In the third quarter of 2026, Annaly’s book value per share, what it owns minus what it owes for each share, fell $2.29 to $17.86, a loss three times its $0.75 quarterly dividend. Ignoring taxes and dividend reinvestment, someone who bought Annaly at the end of September 2016 for an 11% yield has seen its dividend cut in 2019, 2020, and 2023 and its share price fall 60% by Nov. 18, 2026. Counting every dividend, the investment gained 26%, about 2% a year.

In a recent development, keep a mortgage REIT to a slice of your income portfolio small enough that losing half of it wouldn’t change your prepares, and hold it in an IRA. Most REIT dividends don’t get the lower tax rate on qualified dividends, so outside an IRA they’re taxed at your regular rate, after a 20% deduction. In a traditional IRA they aren’t taxed until you withdraw, and a Roth IRA’s qualified withdrawals are tax-free.

Before you buy one, add its last four quarterly dividends to the year’s change in book value per share, both listed in its earnings releases. A negative total means the dividends didn’t cover the drop in book value.

Find an account to hold it in among the best places to open an IRA.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pick one of the largest U.S. banks for its branches and ATMs if you want in-person help wherever you live or move. Then set up enough direct deposit to waive the monthly checking fee, and keep your savings in a high-yield savings account, which pays far more than a branch giant’s basic savings account.

Six of the 10 largest U.S. banks run more than 1,900 branches each, according to the Federal Reserve’s quarterly ranking of commercial banks by assets. Savings is where those branch-heavy giants fall short.

U.S. Bank’s Bank Smartly Savings, for one, pays a standard rate of 0.05% APY, or annual percentage yield, a fraction of the 0.39% national average savings rate the FDIC reports.

It has been revealed that two giants with small branch networks are the exceptions. Marcus, Goldman Sachs’s online bank, pays 3.50% APY on savings, and Capital One pays 3.20% on 360 Performance Savings, both with no monthly fee.

The FDIC’s quarterly count of insured banks and savings institutions stood at 4,238 at the end of June 2026, fewer than a quarter of the 18,033 at the end of 1985.

These were the 10 largest by assets on the Fed’s ranking as of June 30, 2026:.

Sources indicate that reach comes first. A bank with branches and ATMs near your home, your job, and your next address saves you trips and out-of-network ATM fees, and a teller can take a cash deposit or sort out a problem in person. That reach is the reason to keep your checking at one.

Keeping your checking, savings, and investments at one giant earns perks. BofA Rewards waives monthly fees on Bank of America checking and savings once your combined three-month average balance reaches $30,000, counting its deposit accounts and Merrill investments. At that level it also adds 25% to the rewards on eligible credit cards, rising to 75% at $1 million, so the perks matter only if your investments or large balances sit there too.

It has been revealed that checking bonuses are another draw. Chase pays new Total Checking customers $400 after $1,000 in direct deposits within 90 days of enrolling in the offer.

Recent findings suggest that checking fees come first. Chase Total Checking costs $15 a month unless you meet a waiver, such as $500 a month in electronic deposits like a paycheck. PNC’s Virtual Wallet costs $7 a month unless you meet one of its waivers.

Basic savings carries a fee too. Chase, Wells Fargo, and PNC charge $5 a month on it and Bank of America $8, unless you meet a waiver such as keeping $300 in the account ($500 at Bank of America). That’s another reason to keep your savings elsewhere.

Overdraft fees vary. Chase charges $34 per transaction once your balance is more than $50 below zero, up to three fees, or $102, a business day. It waives the fee if your balance is back within $50 of zero when the next business day ends. Citibank, Capital One’s 360 Checking, and Wells Fargo’s Clear Access Banking charge no overdraft fees, so pick one of those if your balance often runs close to zero.

Use the giant for checking. Have your paycheck deposited there to meet the fee waiver, keep about a month of bills in the account, and set a low-balance alert so you see a shortfall before it becomes an overdraft.

Move the rest to a high-yield savings account at another bank, linked to your checking for transfers.

At 3% APY, $10,000 earns $300 in a year, against $5 at 0.05%.

Pick your savings account from the best high-yield savings accounts.

  • I’ve been interested in optimization and trying to get the most out of my body and mind since I was a little kid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a man of Science, I’m supposed to hide my enthusiasm about this somewhat controversial subject, and instead direct you only to the peer-reviewed studies.

But man, I feel like I’ve stumbled upon the fountain of youth here. And the more I dig into the details and the hype and controversy surrounding the field of Hormone Replacement therapy, the more I need to share the word about it to my fellow middle-aged people (both men and women).

I’ve been interested in optimization and trying to get the most out of my body and mind since I was a little kid. I started vacuuming up all the training and nutrition books and magazines I could find while I was just a teenager, and that field still remains a favorite of mine over 30 years later. And if you’re a long-time reader here you’ve been reminded plenty of times of this interest, because health has always been the very heart of Mustachianism.

But a funny thing has been happening in the last ten years: even as I kept honing the healthy living habits and trying my best to improve, there seemed to be a force pulling me back almost as hard. So despite working a bit harder and smarter every year, I still felt myself riding a gradually declining tide of energy, motivation, and physical stamina.

“Perhaps this is just what it means to grow old”, I thought to myself,.

“But I’m still gonna keep fighting it!”.

Yet there was one thing that didn’t quite fit. Why was I having this decline in energy, when some of my older friends weren’t? And why was I still seeing people out there in their 50s, 60s and well beyond doing things that I felt too tired to do today?

Recent findings suggest that one of these tireless friends is a guy named Kevin, who is the personification of the highly energetic successful middle-aged man. He’s a semi-retired serial entrepreneur (and extreme rock climber) who lives in Boulder. And through an interesting twist of fate, in April of 2025 he invited me out for a hike right around the time I was doing all this wondering. And during this hike (and climb) he told me about his latest venture, a boutique men’s health tech giant that specializes in helping men just like us get their youth back through the process of testosterone replacement therapy.

According to recent reports, long story short: his ideas planted a seed in my head, which led to a bunch of research and a growing interest in trying TRT myself. I had of course heard about the process, but for some reason never considered doing it until I heard Kevin’s enthusiasm: he had been on it for several years, and according to him it is a “night and day difference” in all the things you want in life: energy, focus, thinking speed, and of course physical health.

Another convenient twist of fate is that I happen to be dating an REI doctor – a Reproductive Endocrinologist and Infertility specialist who has two board certifications in exactly the relevant bodily systems that are affected by these hormones. And while she was initially skeptical that I needed more Testosterone (and in her practice she regularly sees the downsides of men taking the stuff too early in life and thus compromising their own fertility), she has followed along and helped me learn at each step of this process, eventually becoming fully in support of the program.

According to recent reports, so I signed up as a test customer for Kevin’s new company, which is called Bolt Health. I worked with their doctor to get a baseline blood test and review my numbers compared to all the past tests I’ve collected, and as it turned out, my levels had been dropping consistently over the years, and the latest test was by far the lowest ever.

Even more telling, my age-related drop in Testosterone was correlating perfectly with my decline in energy and motivation:.

The next step was a prescription for a tiny daily dose of supplemental T, which arrived at my house the next week along with instructions for how to use it. And so began the journey.

Now let’s jump forward seven months to the present day as I write this.

Sources indicate that and wow, what a great year it has been! I only wish I had known and tried this a few years earlier, because I’m getting a lot more out of my life.

Sources indicate that it’s not a night-and-day difference for me, but more like a 50% boost in overall youthfulness and energy. The biggest subjective change is that I just don’t have sucky tired days anymore, which was the main problem with my life before: wasting too much of my precious freedom due to not having the energy to enjoy it.

According to recent reports, this is why I’ve become somewhat of an evangelist for hormone replacement therapy for people from about age 45 onwards. It won’t work for everyone – if your levels are already pretty high, you don’t get the same boost. Two of my male friends tried TRT and quit because they didn’t notice any benefit. But these same two guys already had plenty of energy to begin with, which is usually a sign that the body has what it needs.

It turns out I am very late to this party. Although Testosterone supplementation started out as a niche practice in the 1940s, from the 2010s onward it has been everywhere.

TRT is the reason you see every actor suddenly showing up buff overnight for their superhero roles and it’s also why so many of today’s CEOs don’t look anything like yesterday’s CEOs.

Industry observers note that in many cases, it has gone too far with young men using it just to gain muscle for the beach or the football field, and questionable online providers (aka “Prescription Mills”) handing out prescriptions to anyone with a valid credit card – with profit as their sole motive. It became overhyped in certain pockets of Bro Culture, where every Bro eventually receives the advice “Bro! You need to get on the T!” from another Bro, and therefore does it. And some of this reputation surely contributed to my own skepticism.

But there’s a lot of valid science behind TRT, if you’re the right candidate and you take the right dosage. And because of that, I feel it is probably under-hyped in my own demographic, the Nerdy Tech Worker Semi Retired Dad contingent. And that’s why I’m writing this blog post, because there are a lot of us out there.

It has been revealed that many of us just tend to work with what we were given, and accept that aging means slowing down. And for those of us already enjoying an early retirement, we have the option of unlimited rest and recuperation time, so who really cares if we get tired a bit more often? After all, what better way to flex one’s wealth than with a decadent Tuesday Afternoon Nap while everyone else is stuck in the office?

Recent findings suggest that while this seemingly healthy attitude has a lot of positive aspects, it can also mask a real problem which may be easily fixable. Because sometimes, the only thing that’s even better than an afternoon nap, is having the energy and motivation to go out for an afternoon hike, bike ride or adventure with friends. More energy is also pretty darned useful if you’re still raising kids or trying to do well in your career as a person over 45.

How it Actually Works (and What Happened to Me).

In a recent development, distilling all of the fluffy discussion above into the simplest possible answer: TRT means using a tiny needle to inject a few drops of clear liquid just below the surface of your skin. And you do this by yourself at home, ideally once every morning.

Here’s one of the baby needles I use for my daily dose.The typical serving is less than one tenth of a milliliter, which is only a few drops.

Recent findings suggest that and while the term “needle” sounds scary to some, this is very different from the monstrosities they use to draw blood from your veins. This one is so miniature that you don’t need special training to use it, and you usually don’t even feel it.

So I began doing this to myself on May 1st of this year, while keeping a daily journal of my results along the way. The results seemed to be almost immediate in all the promised areas, but I know how powerful the Placebo Effect can be so I kept my skeptic’s hat on to see what would happen in the long run.

I was seeing increased energy and motivation as well as lean weight gain through the whole spring and summer, but I remember the first truly shocking observation happened during a mountain vacation in July. I was part of a multi-family trip with lively adults, chaotic kids, early mornings, late nights with a few drinks, very intense high altitude sunshine and nonstop physical activities. It was just the type of situation that would drain my energy pretty promptly in the past.

But on day three I went out on a solo mountain bike ride to explore the area, and as I was climbing a long ascent with the blazing sun cooking me from every angle I just somehow kept having plenty of energy to keep climbing. Then I came down and joined the group for a few games of full-sun pickleball, biked back up the mountain to our cabin, and the story of unlimited energy went on from there.

“Hot Damn”, I thought to myself, “I don’t know whose youthful and tireless body I have inherited here but I’d sure like to keep it!”.

In August, the Bolt Health program scheduled a follow-up blood test for me and sure enough, my Testosterone levels had been boosted from 415 to 730ng/dL, bringing me from the low side of normal to the higher side.

Many labs define “normal” as anywhere between 300 and 1000, which seems strange to me given the huge effect this hormone has on your wellbeing. It’s a bit like saying “Most cars have between 90 and 300 horsepower, so it doesn’t really matter what engine you have”.

I mean yeah, either one will still get you down the road, but which one would you rather be driving?

Sources indicate that since then, it has just been more of the same good results. My improvements ramped up and then just stayed there – so I’m operating at a upcoming, much higher and more enjoyable level of functioning. Energy and motivation are no longer a problem, and I even find myself willing to make longer-term plans again (before this everything beyond same-day planning felt overwhelming). And my body seems to just want to gain strength and size with any excuse. Heavy weights feel lighter and the hard manual labor I still like to spend my time on feels easier for longer. It’s nice to be young again!

So Why Doesn’t Everyone Do This?

Recent findings suggest that when you dig into the details, hormone replacement is mired in a soup of both real and incorrect information about both its benefits and its risks. And then our well-meaning medical establishment locks this whole container of soup deep in the cabinet with a label that states, “Needs Further Study”. But if you summarize the findings on both sides of the glitch, you’ll see this:.

Stuff you should do BEFORE trying TRT:.

It has been revealed that the modern American Lifestyle is a Testosterone and Health Crusher. It’s a miracle that anybody feels good ever with the crap that people do to their bodies. So if you’re not already doing all the simple, natural, outdoor things that naturally boost your health, energy, and hormone levels, you’ll want to start with these first. You can find a pretty complete list on my oft-cited Badassity Tracker page.

Recent findings suggest that since I was already doing all of these things pretty consistently, I felt ready to take the next step and at least consider hormone supplementation. But wait, there’s more!

Many of the problems above are more likely to appear when the body is flooded with too much testosterone. In the bad old days, TRT was administered by sticking a pellet beneath your skin or injecting a large amount into the butt which then gets used up over the next several weeks. One friend recounted a story of extreme moodiness when the pellet was first implanted, ramping down to tiredness by the time the hormone was all gone.

More modern providers like Bolt have fixed this problem by breaking the dose into much smaller servings which you administer each day. The idea is that your levels remain stable, and you need a lot less overall which reduces side effects.

For my part, I have not had any of the negative side effects because I was a pretty ideal candidate in the first place: 50 years old with depressed Testosterone levels but an otherwise healthy lifestyle and no risk factors.

My hope in sharing this article is to be transparent and hopefully take some of the stigma out of this subject of other people who might benefit. Because in our modern over-connected world, everybody has an opinion on your life, even when you didn’t ask them.

And it’s not just men – many women in this same age group benefit from Estrogen replacement (and there are even interesting stories about female testosterone supplementation in certain situations as this author shares). The point is that aging is normal, but in some cases there’s a pretty easy way to make it slower.

The great news is that Testosterone itself is a cheap and widely available substance, typically under $50 per month even for people like me without conventional insurance or drug coverage. The expensive part (here in the US) is just the doctor stuff – consultations, blood tests, ongoing analysis and prescription renewals and so on.

The organization that I used is positioned as a premium provider, bundling these services along with a bunch of other men’s health perks and deliveries for a few hundred dollars, which is expensive relative to most other parts of my budget, but still cheap if I consider the life and financial benefits of being 20-50% more energetic and productive.

If you want to be on this program, your final decision will hinge on your income, insurance coverage if applicable, whether your existing doctor can already help you, and how much service and advice you’re willing to pay for.

Note: I decided not to become a Bolt health affiliate because I wanted to write this article without conflict of interest. And I can honestly say, Bolt’s product and service seem great to me because I know and trust the people who run it. But  it’s also the only one I’ve tried. So I don’t know much about the competition and there may be other good options out there. At the very minimum, you can always try one service and switch to another if you don’t like the first one.

Industry observers note that I’ve got lots more to say on money and early retirement, and lots of interesting projects in the works now too. So I’m thankful to have stumbled upon this booster for all aspects of life, so I can do more of everything else, for even more decades than I had expected.

I wish this same type of good fortune for you, however you create it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jost Kobusch is back in Nepal, preparing for the fourth round of his Everest project.
  • Industry observers note that “If I am good at something, it’s planning,” the 34-year-old German told ExplorersWeb.
  • It has been revealed that kobusch arrived in Kathmandu two weeks ago, together with friends Nicolas Scheidtweiler, Manuela Brummer, and photographer Alex Pichon.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jost Kobusch is back in Nepal, preparing for the fourth round of his Everest project. His long-term goal is to climb solo in winter, without oxygen, self-supported, and via the Lho La and the West Ridge.

Industry observers note that “If I am good at something, it’s planning,” the 34-year-old German told ExplorersWeb. In this case, his strategy is to arrive at the mountain in the best shape possible, physically and mentally.

It has been revealed that kobusch arrived in Kathmandu two weeks ago, together with friends Nicolas Scheidtweiler, Manuela Brummer, and photographer Alex Pichon. The group soon moved to Manang in the Annapurna region and began acclimatizing in the Chulu range.

Recent findings suggest that jost Kobusch (in yellow) scouts around Manang. Photo: Alex Pichon.

Sources indicate that the strategy was to spend a few nights at altitude and traverse the four Chulu peaks, all above 6,000m. “[However,] expeditions rarely unfold exactly as expected,” Kobusch admitted.

A member in the team felt exhausted after reaching the summit of the second peak, and the group abandoned the traverse there. “At least, we traversed from the summit of Chulu Far East (6,059m) to the top of Chulu East (6,444m) from the southeast,” Kobusch mentioned. He says their line between the two peaks was latest.

Sources indicate that the line followed by Kobusch and his team up Chulu East. Photo: Alex Pichon.

It has been revealed that their next proposal will be to climb a 7,000m peak in the area before Kobusch moves to the Khumbu in November. “I want to reach 8,000m, but on a different mountain than Everest, before the beginning of winter,” he stated.

He wants to be completely acclimatized by the time he starts working on Everest on December 22, the start of calendar winter. Kobusch will have two photographers in Base Camp, but he will climb alone.

Acclimatization in Manang, Photo: Alex Pichon.

In a recent development, “I need to be able to move efficiently, make good decisions when I’m tired, manage risk alone, and stay comfortable in an environment where very small mistakes can have very serious consequences,” Kobusch recently wrote on social media. He says that so far, all is going well. “I’m feeling good, I’ve done my homework, and I will start again on Everest better prepared than ever.”.

Kobusch has attempted winter Everest solo on three previous occasions, always via the Lho La and the West Ridge, thus avoiding venturing alone into the Khumbu Icefall.

In his first attempt in 2019-20, he reached the West Shoulder and pushed above 7,300m. On the second attempt in 2021-22, high winds didn’t let him go beyond 6,400m. He planned to try again the following year, but he caught dengue fever while training in Nepal and had to cancel.

It has been revealed that once recovered, he soloed Denali in February-March 2023. Everest had to wait one more year, this time due to a back injury. On the third attempt in 2024-25, he reached his highest point yet: 7,537m on December 27.

Kobusch’s highest point is shown with a green circle, and the Hornbein Couloir is the pink line on the 3D map by RealityMaps.

“The chances of success are not particularly high,” he recently wrote. “If I had to put a number on it, I would say around 20%. But that does not make the attempt meaningless. If anything, it is part of what makes it interesting.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that have a government photo ID, your Social Security number or IRS taxpayer ID (ITIN), your current address, and money for the opening deposit ready before you open a bank account.
  • Banks use those details to confirm who you are, and an online application may ask questions based on public records, such as a past address.
  • Industry observers note that for the ID number, a Social Security number isn’t the only option.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that have a government photo ID, your Social Security number or IRS taxpayer ID (ITIN), your current address, and money for the opening deposit ready before you open a bank account. With those in hand, applying online or at a branch is quick. Then use the first week to set up direct deposit and balance alerts.

Banks use those details to confirm who you are, and an online application may ask questions based on public records, such as a past address. If you can’t finish that check online, you may have to call or visit a branch, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation explains.

Industry observers note that for the ID number, a Social Security number isn’t the only option. An ITIN, the IRS tax ID for people who need one but can’t get a Social Security number, works too. Some banks also accept a foreign passport or a consular ID as your photo ID. If you’re upcoming to the country, ask what the bank takes first.

Pick a checking account for everyday spending, a savings account for money you’re setting aside, or both, then apply online or at a branch, where a banker may ask to see your ID.

Sources indicate that if you’ve moved since your ID was issued, have proof of your current address ready, such as a recent bill or your lease. Banks may also check your banking history, and an unpaid overdraft at an old bank can get you turned down. If that happens, ask which reporting company the bank used, such as ChexSystems, and get your free report from it to dispute any error.

Picture a 19-year-old moving off her parents’ account. She opens checking and savings on her phone in one sitting, then gives her employer the routing and account numbers from the app for direct deposit.

In the first week, make the opening deposit by transfer, mobile check deposit, or cash, and order the debit card if one isn’t on its way.

Recent findings suggest that last, turn down overdraft coverage, which lets a one-time debit card purchase or ATM withdrawal go through for a fee when your balance falls short. Without your opt-in, the bank can’t charge that fee, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau notes. A check or recurring payment can still overdraw the account for a fee, so set a low-balance alert for an amount above your largest automatic payment.

Compare the best checking accounts to pick where you’ll open yours.

The Japanese pair headed to the 7,140m peak in September, and we heard no further news of them. After a major storm hit Nepal’s mountains three weeks ago, we presumed they had retreated. But now it seems they did not. They have been out of touch since October 15, after encountering severe weather conditions during their attempt to climb the peak, According to News on Nepal.

Sources indicate that hidesuke Taneishi, left, and Tetsu Hashimoto, right, with a support team member in Kathmandu earlier this week. Photo: Cosmo Adventure.

The Russian team that reached the mountain earlier this month reportedly found no sign of the Japanese climbers on the peak. Bad weather forced the Russians down from their summit attempt at 6,800m.

Recent findings suggest that A helicopter search-and-rescue operation is now underway, Manang Chief District Officer Mukti Prasad Khanal has confirmed. Today, high-altitude helicopters and drones successfully recovered some of their gear, including trekking poles, near 7,050m, but the climbers themselves remain missing.

Gangapurna West is also known as Asapurna or Peak Lachenal.

The three-man Russian team returned to Everest’s West Ridge but found the route even more difficult than they expected. After two days of struggle, they’re heading back to Base Camp.

On October 20, Andrei Vasiliev, Serguey Kondrashkin, and Vitaly Shipilov went back up to the Lho La and pitched their tent on the wide plateau beyond. They still had time to fix more rope higher up.

“We moved…over terrain we’d already covered on the previous rotation,” the climbers texted to team member Natalya Belyankina, who had to abandon the expedition due to illness.

In a recent development, “The weather is good: sunny, with light winds, but cold,” they noted. “Progress was painfully slow today due to heavy packs and a persistent cough,” the climbers noted later.

On Wednesday, they hoped to reach 7,500m, spend the night there, check the route ahead, and then retreat to the plateau. However, they didn’t get as far as they had planned.

In a recent development, “We didn’t cover much ground today,” leader Andrei Vsiliev texted Anna Piunova of The Mountain Club. “The route is no walk in the park. We have to climb steep snowy slopes that conceal rock sections underneath.”.

Sources indicate that to make things worse, they found no suitable bivy spots at their highest point, so they had to retreat to a place where they could pitch their tent for the night. Today, they were just too exhausted to keep going.

“We’re heading down; we’re sick and need to recover,” Vasiliev told Belyankina. “We can barely keep moving.”.

It has been revealed that you’ll save more on your wedding reception’s food and drink by changing when and how the meal is served than by trimming the menu one dish at a time. Ask your caterer to price a brunch or afternoon buffet with beer and wine against a sit-down evening dinner with a full bar.

In a recent development, those two quotes cover the second-biggest share of the average wedding budget. In The Knot’s wedding budget breakdown, food and drink take 24%, behind only the venue and rentals at 29%.

A brunch or lunch reception usually costs less than dinner, because the menu is lighter and guests drink less earlier in the day. A buffet usually costs less than a plated meal brought to each seat, since it needs fewer servers, though it takes more food. Family-style platters, passed around each table, cost somewhere between the two. Food stations can cost more than a plated meal, because each station needs staff to run it.

In The Knot’s 2026 Real Weddings Study, catering averaged $80 a guest at 2025 weddings, and alcohol averaged $2,800 a wedding. Say you’re feeding 120 guests, and your caterer quotes $110 a guest in food and drink for a plated evening dinner with a full open bar, and $70 for an afternoon buffet with beer and wine. The afternoon buffet costs $4,800 less than the evening dinner. Every guest you take off the list saves the full per-guest price as well.

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Donovan Rice got into thru-hiking almost by accident.
  • Recent findings suggest that “I thought, there’s no way somebody can walk from Mexico to Canada.
  • From there, it was a slippery slope.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Donovan Rice got into thru-hiking almost by accident. Already outdoorsy, he graduated from long hikes to planning to climb all 53 of Colorado’s 14,000’ers (mountains above 14,000 feet, or 4,267m). While researching which peaks required overnight camping, he realized that some people’s hikes just keep going.

Recent findings suggest that “I thought, there’s no way somebody can walk from Mexico to Canada. That’s just ridiculous,” Rice explained. “I fell in love with that idea.”.

From there, it was a slippery slope. First came the Pacific Crest Trail (PCT), from the Mexican border in California to the Canadian border in British Columbia. Then he did the Continental Divide Trail (CDT), tracing the Rocky Mountains from New Mexico to the Montana-Canada border. Before he knew it, he had a trail name — Iceman —and was working the gig economy to free up time for wilderness adventures.

But that’s where most people’s slippery slope levels out. Hiking the 4,988km CDT is as meaty a project as most of us can imagine. But for Rice, it only opened the floodgates. He was fascinated by everything that didn’t make it into famous routes, especially the ridges and mountains he passed in his home state of Colorado that were just off trail.

In a recent development, “There’s all this stuff the CDT doesn’t hit because it is following the Continental Divide,” he told ExplorersWeb. “So when I got to the end of the Colorado section, about 700 miles, I was thinking, man, if there were a 2,000-mile version of that, it would be my dream thru-hike. Just that non-stop, relentless brutality that is Colorado.”.

Recent findings suggest that colorado has 14,000′ peaks but also deserts. Photo: Donovan Rice.

Rice started thinking about a massive thru-hike loop of the state. His idea was to stitch together existing trails and form latest ones where necessary.

“I dropped a load of pins across the areas in Colorado I wanted to visit, then I pulled out a public lands layer of the map to see how I might connect the areas,” he explained. “The three core design philosophies were beauty, breadth, and epicness. I wanted to see beautiful views, I wanted to cover as much of Colorado’s diversity as possible, and I wanted to take the most iconic and epic route possible.”.

Sources indicate that unlike places like the UK, there is no “right to roam” in Colorado, so connecting the route to avoid private land was tricky. Occasionally, he had to link bits of public land and sections of trail in the “least worst way,” with short road walks when private property appeared to halt progress.

According to recent reports, as he tacked on mountain peaks and the national parks he wanted to explore, his route swelled to a monstrous 3,000km+. His itinerary now included all 11 of Colorado’s national forests, three of its national parks, 13 14,000’ers and 47 13,000’ers.

Sources indicate that “This is not an efficient route,” Rice admits. “You could walk the full perimeter of Colorado and then hike the Colorado Trail [an existing 885km trail from Waterton Canyon near Denver to Durango], and then still have kilometers left over [to complete the loop].”.

Industry observers note that the Great Colorado Route. Photo: Donovan Rice.

In a recent development, the route looked epic on paper, but Rice still needed to prove it could actually be thru-hiked. After months of planning, Rice set off on his Great Colorado Route from Gunnison National Park on May 14, 2026. He traveled ultra-light, carrying just six kilos of gear, with just a quilt instead of a sleeping bag and a tarp rather than a tent.

Industry observers note that “I wanted it to be lightweight enough that I could be nimble on the mountains while doing these technical traverses,” remarked Rice. Traveling light was wise. Rice’s Great Colorado Route is challenging, with plenty of scrambling and sustained time at altitude.

In a recent development, “The crux might be between Bailey and Rocky Mountain National Park. You go over the Mount Evans Wilderness, two 14,000’ers, hop on the Front Range across several 13,000’ers, and then across the Tenmile Range, and then the absolutely brutal Gore Range.”.

Recent findings suggest that rice spent 141 days tramping his trail, eventually finishing on October 1 after 3,252km. While he describes the route as “definitely not beginner-friendly” — due to plenty of cross-country terrain, off-trail navigation, and route-finding — it doesn’t require mountaineering skills.

In a recent development, “For me, the real sweet spot is Class three scrambling,” he says. “Once you get up to Class four, it starts getting really scary, and I had no tolerance at all for true Class five rock climbing.”.

According to recent reports, however, he did pack an ice ax, micro-spikes, snow gaiters, and a lightweight helmet to protect against rockfall. He also made an effort to structure the route to provide relief between the most challenging sections, giving the trail an ebb and flow, and potential hikers time to decompress.

The Ballard to La Junta traverse. Photo: Donovan Rice.

Recent findings suggest that overall, his focus on scenic beauty over contrived difficulty helped keep the route somewhat accessible. This is vital because Rice hopes that other hikers will give it a go. He is building a website that maps the route, segment by segment, with GPS coordinates to help future hikers find the best places to camp or alternative paths depending on trail conditions. This is a May-through-October trail, but Rice stresses that it is unrealistic to expect perfect conditions for four and a half months.

“This is one of those routes where bailouts will have to happen,” Rice explained. “You’ll have to take a low route or an alternate. I’m hoping to revisit some of the areas in the future and establish some of these alternative routes.”.

It has been revealed that he aims to get all 29 segments of the initial route fully mapped on The Great Colorado website by the end of the year. It’s a big project, almost as big as the hike itself.

“I need to see how many people will actually give it a try. People can do segments. I’d love to see more thru-hikers do this, but the significant challenge is that I think the majority of thru-hikers will look at this and think ‘that’s above my pay grade’.”.

The Castles, Colorado. Photo: Donovan Rice.

According to recent reports, once he finishes the website, the level of interest might dictate his next steps. “I don’t know what level of formal recognition I want to try for. Do I want to try to get it codified? Or should it stay unofficial and remain just some cool thing someone did that published information on how to do it yourself.”.

Whether or not his Great Colorado Route ever gains the name recognition of the CDT or PCT, Rice has authored something unique, and in a world full of rehashes and copycats, that makes it special.

In a recent development, rice looking down on Island Lake from Ulysses S. Grant Peak. Photo: Donovan Rice.

Bring in a professional when the buying feels compulsive, when you find hidden accounts or debt, or when the spending threatens the bills. To get there, give your florist a color palette instead of a list of must-have blooms, and ask what local growers will have in season the month of your wedding.

Then use each arrangement twice. Ask a friend to carry the ceremony arrangements to the reception during cocktail hour, and set the bridesmaids’ bouquets in vases of water on the head table.

Industry observers note that leave the bouquets and boutonnieres to the florist, and make simple centerpieces yourself from bulk flowers and greenery, which Costco and Sam’s Club sell online. On tables that don’t need flowers, set out candles or potted plants. Doing all the flowers yourself means taking on the florist’s prep, from stripping thorns to giving each stem a fresh cut. Try it only with helpers and refrigerated space lined up for the day before the wedding.

Before you sign with a florist, ask for a second quote with in-season flowers and the ceremony arrangements reused, then compare the two line by line.

  • Don’t get me wrong, it’s a great thing for the 73 million people who currently draw benefits, and it provides an essential safety net for many who don’t have much income from anywhere else.
  • According to recent reports, but for those of us leaving the workplace in our 30 and 40s, Social Security is just a fuzzy concept in the very distant future.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the world of very early retirement, we tend to ignore one of the most important things for normal retirees: the Social Security program.

Don’t get me wrong, it’s a great thing for the 73 million people who currently draw benefits, and it provides an essential safety net for many who don’t have much income from anywhere else.

According to recent reports, but for those of us leaving the workplace in our 30 and 40s, Social Security is just a fuzzy concept in the very distant future. We aren’t thinking about money that eases us into our Golden Years, we need something that starts working now. Plus we’d rather not rely on our government keeping its promises that far into the future.

Sources indicate that those were my thoughts in 2005, when I was just a young retiree myself. But a funny thing happens when time passes: you get older. And you realize that there are plenty of other older people around too. And suddenly, Social Security is an important subject after all, that many people would like to know more about. But there is an endless pile of conflicting opinions:.

Industry observers note that but when I did the math on all of this, I realized that it’s more confusing than it needs to be. Because when it comes to deciding on how Social Security fits into your retirement strategy, it really boils down to only one number:.

The Net Present Value of your future lifetime stream of Social Security payments.

That little piece of math jargon might not mean much if you don’t have fond memories of  Economics 101 class. But don’t worry, it’s easy to understand if you think of these two extremes:.

Industry observers note that if you want to retire in your 30s like I did, the value of your future Social Security is pretty close to zero. Even if the government keeps all of its promises, those payments are so far in the future that you need to save a full retirement ‘stash to get through the three decades until it kicks in.

On the other hand, if you’re already over 60 years old, contributed to Social Security throughout your long career and have a low cost of living, you may be eligible for payments that already meet all your needs.

In this situation, you are set for life. Social Security will in theory cover all your needs and rise automatically with inflation, so you don’t have to save any additional money.

In between these two extremes, the math gets interesting. Because while most people assume Social Security is useless until you reach full eligibility, the real story is that you can think of it as a chunk of money that you already have right now, which reduces the amount of saving you have to do on your own.

And there’s an easy way to calculate it, with an extremely useful thing called the Net Present Value calculation.

There’s an actual formula for this, but don’t worry you don’t have to memorize it because you can just have any Internet calculator, AI tool or spreadsheet do the math for you.

Sources indicate that first let’s calculate the value a young couple might get if they do this calculation at 30 years old. We just have to make a few assumptions to have numbers plug into the formula:.

Recent findings suggest that when you plug in all the numbers and calculate this (the Net Present Value of a 30 year stream of income), the first number you’ll get is $667,166. But that’s not the final answer – that is how much you’d need if you wanted the payments to start right now.

The final step is applying a simpler version of the formula a second time, to account for the fact that you don’t need the money until 32 years from now:.

At that point, you end up with a number around $98,280. But what does this mean?

It means that if you stuck $98k into an investment account today and let it compound for 32 years, at that point it would be massive enough to provide a stream of $4000 payments for the following 30 years. And this even takes future inflation into account!It also means that the 30 year old retirees can mark an imaginary $98k onto their “net worth” spreadsheet and save that much less. Or at least think of it as a nice safety margin.

If you’re new to money and math, that may sound like sorcery, but if you’ve been investing for long enough you will understand that it really does work that way. So let’s re-run the example for a couple who is already 62 years old, and needs a $5000 income starting right now, that still needs to last 30 years.

That NPV calculation looks like this:.

And the answer is right around $834,000.

In a recent development, what this means, is that if they invested $834,000 into a fund that paid out 6% per year for 30 years before running dry, they’d get that exact same $5000 monthly income. And it would keep up with inflation.

It has been revealed that now that we’ve seen these examples from the extreme ends of the spectrum, we can see how this applies in a more typical situation. Here’s one that is loosely based on one from a real person I worked with last year:.

Shane Survivor is 55 and he has been through some hard times. He lost most of his savings in a business blowup a few years back, but really wishes he could still retire soon. His financial picture:.

According to recent reports, most financial advisors would tell him to tough it out and  just keep working until he hits Social Security eligibility. At least 62 to get the minimum benefits, but maybe even longer to get to Full Retirement Age (67) or even until 70 to get the maximum benefit.

Industry observers note that but wait! Let’s do the math because who wants to work another fifteen years when you’re already tired of working at 55!

Shane logs into the Social Security website SSA.gov and uses the online tool to calculate what his payout will be. I just did this myself so we can use my numbers:.

Let’s start by calculating the Net Present Value of each of these three options for our 55-year old friend:.

Whoa wait a minute, that’s a counterintuitive result! Am I really telling you that it’s actually less valuable to work longer so you can get the higher benefits? The answer is yes, for people who understand the concepts of “investing” and “the time value of money”.

Industry observers note that to really understand this, just imagine what would happen if you started taking those payments as early as possible (age 62) and tossed them into an index fund, earning 6% after inflation on average. After the first year, you’d already have about $24,300 and you’d still be piling in that extra two grand per month and the whole snowball would be starting to compound.

Industry observers note that by the time your more patient friends started drawing $2796 payments five years later, you’d already have over $137,000. It’s such a big lead that the 67-year-old will never catch up.

But let’s go back to Shane’s real situation and see if he can retire:.

So the answer is no, not quite yet. But he’s closer than it looks: every year of additional work will have a triple effect because it will:.

As soon as his combined ‘stash investment income plus the Social Security payment reach $3000 per month, he’s done.

According to recent reports, and of course, any additional tricks he can apply like streamlining his spending and boosting his income, will make this even faster. I’d give him about three years before reaching liftoff.

So how can YOU use this information to speed up your own retirement?

The net effect of Social Security is that it should help you worry a little less and work a little less. The worrying part should benefit everyone, and the working part is kind of a sliding scale:.

Can we just put this in ONE SIMPLE TABLE based on some reasonable assumptions?

For example as a 51-year-old, I can look at my number of roughly $350,000 and say yeah, that’s quite a big boost – enough to buy an entire house in many areas of the country or enough to fund multiple lifetimes of high-end groceries. And until now I had never even considered it as part of my retirement savings!

Frequently Asked (or Complained) Questions.

Now that we’ve covered the facts, I can already hear the complaints coming.

What if Social Security is canceled or greatly reduced by the time I reach that age?

Yeah, it might happen, but it’s also a top priority for most voters in our aging population. So it’s hard for politicians to make cuts. What is more likely is that the benefits will be cut for wealthier people. And if you find yourself in that camp (as I do), you won’t actually need the payments.

In a recent development, sure, it’s not “fair”, but you know what? I can think of more fun ways to enjoy the fact that I’m a rich person rather than complaining about how some government program is “unfair”, and so can you.

Nobody can live on just a Social Security check!

First of all, millions of people do. In fact, last time I checked my own annual spending it was under $30k, most of it on optional luxuries, which is less than my expected payout!

But more importantly, most of us won’t have to, because we are also investing healthy sums on our own.

I’m still scared and worried about something else!

Now this is the root of the matter. In fact, worry is the root of almost all concerns. And so that’s what we need to focus on in our future work. For some reason, I have managed to live the last twenty years pretty much completely free from financial worries, and I had assumed everyone else was the same way. But it turns out this is not the case, even among people much wealthier and more advantaged than I am.

So in the next article, we need to get into that.

Log yourself into ssa.gov, and if it’s your first time doing that – congratulations! Note that new people will need to create an account, and they’ll guide you to login.gov for that purpose. Don’t fret, it’s very useful to have this account for multiple reasons.

Bonus Materials: the Quirk of Social Security Contributions.

Industry observers note that to illustrate this point, I ran a simulation of two people who each make a $100k salary and contribute accordingly, but one retires after 10 years and that poor second guy works the full 35. Look at the difference in their benefits:.

So the early retiree only worked and contributed about 28% as much as the late retiree. But his benefits are still a much higher 45% of the substantial earner’s payouts. In summary? Social Security provides a mild incentive for slacking.

It has been revealed that one other factor: after retiring earlier, you might still end up contributing more than you think. This is because any income you earn later in life through optional employment (or self employment) will trigger more contributions. In my 21 years of retirement, I have ended up earning and contributing more during about 15 of those years, bringing my average level up much higher than I originally expected.

Even though this has become a long article, it is still far from a complete analysis of the Social Security program. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • The usual blueprint with friends, a restaurant or a bar, comes with a bill every time.
  • Yet what makes time together good is the conversation, the food, and something to do, and none of it needs a restaurant or a bar.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that you can see friends often on a tight budget by making the cheap strategy the usual one. Rotate potlucks and game nights between your homes, and look up free museum days, library events, and park concerts. When the group goes out, pick happy hour, a matinee, or a group rate.

The usual blueprint with friends, a restaurant or a bar, comes with a bill every time. In a group where incomes differ, someone ends up turning down the plan or overspending to keep up.

Yet what makes time together good is the conversation, the food, and something to do, and none of it needs a restaurant or a bar.

It has been revealed that dinner out is the easiest blueprint to swap. In a rotating potluck, a different friend hosts each month and everyone brings a dish. Say dinner out runs $55 a person with tax and tip, and a potluck dish costs $15 to make. A group of six that swaps its monthly restaurant night for a rotating potluck cuts each person’s cost from $55 to $15, a $40 saving every month, and each friend hosts just twice a year.

Sources indicate that game nights, watch parties for a show or a significant game, and cooking or baking together work the same way. Each friend brings a snack, a drink, or an ingredient.

Outside the house, start with what’s free or nearly free:.

Industry observers note that for a paid night out, pick the cheaper time. Happy hour cuts the price of drinks and appetizers, and matinees and discount days cut ticket prices. For bowling or an escape room, ask about a group rate before everyone pays separately. Ask, too, whether a friend’s museum, zoo, or gym membership includes guest passes. Before you book, check for a drink minimum, common at comedy clubs, and for fees that raise the ticket price.

In your group chat this week, pick a date and a host for the first potluck, and have each friend claim a dish so no two people bring the same thing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This morning, rescuers found the bodies of Japanese climbers Hidesuke Taneishi, 40, and Tetsu Hashimoto, 25, on Gangapurna West.

“Both bodies were found at around 6,300m on the south side of Gangapurna West,” the rescue team told The Tourism Times.

Industry observers note that hidesuke Taneishi (left) and Tetsu Hashimoto (right) with a support team member in Kathmandu earlier this week. Photo: Cosmo Adventure.

The climbers were attempting the first ascent of the 7,140m mountain and lost contact on October 15 at approximately 7,050m on their summit push.

In a recent development, A search-and-rescue team has been looking for the pair since October 19. Unfortunately, no one knew where they were on the mountain, or even if they were on the mountain at all. Therefore, the search started at Manang village, with no success.

According to recent reports, the team included helicopter pilot Sobit Gauchan, high-altitude photographer and climber Manish Maharjan, and IFMGA mountain guide Pansang Rinzee Sherpa. The helicopter dropped Maharjan and Rinzee at 5,750m, and from there they used a drone to search the upper slopes. They scouted the northeast and southwest sides of the mountain, and finally found the remains of the Japanese climbers’ higher camp. Today, they found the bodies on the south side.

As for the cause of the accident, Rinzee told ExplorersWeb that their observations of the terrain pointed to a snow slab collapse.

According to recent reports, several teams have attempted Gangapurna West, located next to the Annapurna massif in Manang district, since it opened to foreign teams in 2014. However, none have summited. The mountain is also known as Asapurna or Lachenal Peak.

Team leader Hidesuke Taneishi was nominated for a Piolet d’Or last year after his first ascent of 6,652m Pholesobi Peak, also in Nepal, via a direct route up its vertiginous north face with Hiroki Yamamoto.

Hidesuke Taneishi on the summit of Pholesobi Peak. Photo: Hiroki Yamamoto.

How Much House Can You Afford? Budget the Full Payment, Not the Approval

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (436 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A mortgage approval shows the most you can borrow, not how much house you can afford.
  • Lenders often approve much more than that.
  • Take a couple earning $120,000 a year, or $10,000 a month, with no other debts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A mortgage approval shows the most you can borrow, not how much house you can afford. Base your price range on the full monthly payment, which adds property taxes, homeowners insurance, homeowners association dues, and mortgage insurance to the loan payment. Keep that payment near 28% of your gross income so upkeep and savings still fit.

Lenders often approve much more than that. They go by your debt-to-income ratio, your monthly debt payments as a share of gross income, and Fannie Mae’s rules let that share reach 50%, the upcoming mortgage included.

Take a couple earning $120,000 a year, or $10,000 a month, with no other debts. Assume 10% down, a 7% rate on a 30-year fixed loan, property taxes and homeowners insurance at 1.5% of the price a year, and mortgage insurance at $50 a month per $100,000 borrowed.

Even a lender that caps their debts at 43% of income would approve a $4,300 payment, enough for about a $560,000 home. Holding the full payment near $2,800, or 28%, points them to homes around $365,000, nearly $200,000 below the $560,000 approval.

Price your own payment for the town you’re shopping in.

Industry observers note that next, run a budget test. Add what the home costs beyond the payment, starting with upkeep, which Fannie Mae puts at 1% of its value a year for a newer house and up to 4% for one over 30 years old. Your take-home pay still has to cover retirement contributions and emergency savings.

Then stress-test the number. For three to six months before you buy, save the difference between your rent and the upcoming payment plus upkeep, as a trial run. Rates can rise before you lock one in, so price the payment at a rate one percentage point higher, which lifts the couple’s $2,800 to about $3,030. Last, count how many months of payments your emergency fund covers if a paycheck stops.

The highest price that passes both tests is your ceiling, whatever the approval letter states.

Your Wedding Date Sets the Venue’s Price – Ask for Friday, Sunday & Winter Rates

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, wedding venues charge the most for Saturdays from late spring through fall, and many charge less for a Friday, a Sunday, or a date in their slow months.
  • According to recent reports, venues price by demand, and most of that demand falls in six months of the year.
  • In a recent development, any day but Saturday is one a venue would rather fill at a lower price than leave empty, and so is almost any date in its slow season, usually January through March in much of the country.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, wedding venues charge the most for Saturdays from late spring through fall, and many charge less for a Friday, a Sunday, or a date in their slow months. Before you set your wedding date, ask every venue you’re considering for its prices by day of the week and by month.

According to recent reports, venues price by demand, and most of that demand falls in six months of the year. About three in four weddings take place between May and October, according to The Knot.

In a recent development, any day but Saturday is one a venue would rather fill at a lower price than leave empty, and so is almost any date in its slow season, usually January through March in much of the country. The discount can come off the rental fee or the food-and-drink minimum, the least you must spend on the venue’s catering and bar. Say a venue sets a $10,000 minimum for June Saturdays and $6,500 for February Fridays. Booking a February Friday instead of a June Saturday saves $3,500 before anything else changes, and a brunch or afternoon start can lower the catering bill further.

In a recent development, other vendors vary. Some will lower their rate for a slow date, while others charge the same all year. Hotels near the venue usually charge less in their own slow months, too. That lowers the rate on a room block, the rooms a hotel holds for your guests at a group price.

Find out which dates each venue counts as peak, since some charge Saturday prices for the Sunday before Memorial Day or Labor Day. Then ask your other vendors whether a different date changes their quote.

It has been revealed that weigh what the date costs your guests, too. A Friday or a midweek date means time off work for many of them, a Sunday means a late trip home or a Monday off for anyone traveling in, and winter weather can delay flights and make driving risky. Check the local calendar as well, since a festival or a college graduation weekend can fill nearby hotels and push up room rates.

Ask each venue to quote the same wedding on three dates, a Saturday in your first-choice month, a Friday or Sunday that month, and a Saturday in January, so you can see what moving the date would save.

  • In a recent development, the Mountain Literature award went to Lone Wolf: Walking the Line Between Civilization and Wildness by Adam Weymouth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that every year, the Banff Centre Mountain Film and Book Festival celebrates the best mountain and adventure writing, film, and photography. The literary highlight of this alpine-themed celebration is the Banff Mountain Book Competition, with eight categories and one grand prize. The jury will award the grand prize at the festival, but the category winners have been declared.

First, the two Special Jury Mentions. Jack Plant’s Spirit of the Great Bear showcases his spectacular photography of the Great Bear Forest. Meanwhile, Ian Nicholson’s Glacier Travel & Crevasse Rescue: Essential Skills for Snow Travel does exactly what it says on the tin. “Of all the skill sets required for mountain climbing, perhaps none are as intimidating as glacier travel. But with carefully crafted instructions and illustrations, Nicholson takes us behind the curtain,” jury member Lauren DeLaunay Miller explains.

In a recent development, the Mountain Literature award went to Lone Wolf: Walking the Line Between Civilization and Wildness by Adam Weymouth. Weymouth dives into the place of wild animals in modern Europe, a continent “undergoing profound climatic, environmental, and political changes.”.

Black Bear: A Story of Siblinghood and Survival by Trina Moyles won the Environmental Literature category. “Black Bear seamlessly weaves together two complex storylines, laying bare Moyles’ relationships with her brother and with the wildlife she meets while working in a fire watch tower in Alberta.”.

Industry observers note that the Mountain Article prize, awarded to a magazine piece rather than a book, went to The Misfits by Chad Heddleston. Heddleston chose to profile rock climbing couple Jan and Herb Conn. “These two exist in the spirit and austerity of the pioneering European climbers of the early 20th century. The writing highlights their uniqueness and the integrity of their life choices,” jury member David Chambre mentioned.

Pioneering rock climbers Jan and Herb Conn. Photo: Dwight Deal.

It has been revealed that the Adventure Travel prize went to North to the Future: An Offline Adventure through the Changing Wilds of Alaska by Ben Weissenbach. “Weissenbach — an L.A. native with little prior wilderness experience — treks through the Alaskan tundra with a series of eccentric environmental scientists and returns with a latest perspective on technology and a revitalized sense of wonder for the natural world.”.

Cabin Wild: Alpine Bivouac Huts by Ben Tibbetts won the Guidebook award. “A captivating volume that invites us to see the Alps in a newly introduced light, through an intimate journey around a selection of bivouac huts across Italy, Switzerland, and France,” according to jury member Rob Lovell.

According to recent reports, the Mountain Image award went to Fjell: A Faithful Witness by Orsolya Haarberg. “A highly original book that takes us on a journey through the Norwegian highlands. It is as much an art book as a book about mountains,” explains jury member David Chambre.

In a recent development, finally, The Great Mixed Climbs of Scotland by Guy Robertson & Hamish Frost won the Climbing Literature prize. “The Great Mixed Climbs of Scotland combines stunning photography and evocative essays in a truly spectacular ode to Scottish winter climbing. By profiling crucial routes through the eyes of the climbers who created them, Guy Robertson and Hamish Frost have created an exceptional book.”.

The category-winning authors get cash prizes and a chance to win the grand prize at the festival on November 5.
